claims: Artemis III is currently scheduled to launch in mid-2027.
Artemis III will involve a crewed flight to low-Earth orbit to test docking capabilities between the Orion spacecraft and commercial lunar landers SpaceX Starship or Blue Origin Blue Moon.
The first human landing is now slated for Artemis IV in 2028.
Artemis III's mission goal is to test rendezvous and docking of the crewed Orion capsule with commercial moon landers in Earth orbit.
Artemis III will be launched by NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) from Kennedy Space Center.
Artemis III's crewed landing on the Moon has been deferred to Artemis IV or V in 2028.
Artemis III crew has not yet been announced.
Selection of Artemis III crew is underway.
As of April 2026, NASA has revised the Artemis III mission profile to focus on orbital rendezvous rather than a direct lunar surface landing.
NASA's revision of the Artemis III mission profile follows an announcement by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman on February 27, 2026.
